title: Echo State Networks: A Non-Intrusive Approach to Anomaly Detection in Manufacturing
problem: Anomaly detection in manufacturing processes like GMAW welding requires machine learning models, but many manufacturing environments lack large training datasets and cannot afford extensive preprocessing or feature engineering by subject matter experts.
motivation: Enabling anomaly detection in manufacturing with minimal training data improves product quality and reliability while reducing data collection overhead.
method: Echo State Networks use a recurrent neural network with a fixed random reservoir, training only the readout layer via pseudo-inverse matrix method. The approach analyzes raw power consumption data from welders without manual feature engineering. This training mechanism enables learning from minimal examples, even a single weld.
key_novelty: Echo State Networks achieve effective anomaly detection from a single training example using pseudo-inverse matrix training, enabling practical deployment in manufacturing with severely limited data availability.
contributions: Demonstrates ESNs effectively detect anomalies in GMAW welding using only power consumption measurements
Shows ESNs require minimal training data compared to backpropagation-based models like transformers
Eliminates manual feature engineering by processing raw sensor data directly
Provides comparative analysis showing ESN advantage over transformers in low-data manufacturing scenarios

metrics.accuracy: comparable to transformers with significantly reduced training data requirements

limitations: Scalability to diverse manufacturing processes and real-world deployment challenges not discussed.
primary_theme: Low-data anomaly detection via reservoir computing
